back: A threat can cause harm to a system or its data; a vulnerability is the weakness that a threat can exploit.
Virus: attaches to a host file and needs it run. Worm: copies itself across a network on its own. Trojan: looks useful but hides harmful code; does not copy itself.
Phishing: a fake message tricks the user into giving details. Pharming: the user is redirected to a fake web site even when the correct address is typed.
Ransomware encrypts files and demands payment. Spyware secretly records what the user does; a keylogger records keystrokes.
A flood of requests makes a server unavailable to genuine users; DDoS uses many infected computers. No data need be stolen.
Unpatched software, weak or default passwords, poor configuration, programming flaws (buffer overflow, SQL injection), people and unprotected networks.
Combinations = (number of characters to choose from) ^ (length). Brute-force time = combinations ÷ guesses per second.
User text is joined into a database command, so typed SQL is run; prevented by parameterised queries and input checks.
Tricking people instead of machines into giving away access or information, for example a caller who pretends to be IT support.
